idiomatic.rationale: Standalone OnPush components, signal inputs, control-flow syntax, toSignal and inject() are all current and correct, but route-param fetching, async loading and per-page titles are built on pre-resource RxJS patterns that the v22 docs and official skill now steer away from — several framework features exist for exactly this code.

app/src/app/core/api.service.ts:35 — catchError(() => of(null)) conflates 404 with network/server errors, so a down API renders 'Not found' instead of an error state

app/src/app/pages/pokemon-page.ts:372-379 — plain effect doing DOM scroll work with a bare setTimeout (no cleanup, re-fires on every tables change); docs recommend afterRenderEffect for post-render DOM manipulation
app/src/app/shared/pokemon-card.ts:36-45 — manual .subscribe() in the image-error handler with no takeUntilDestroyed; touches a possibly-detached img and never handles the error callback
app/src/app/pages/home-page.ts:52-57 — every keystroke triggers a router.navigate (replaceUrl) with no debounce; spec-allowed but adds history churn
correctness_risks.rationale: No races found — switchMap is used consistently, fan-out is bounded and cached, 404 pages handled — but the leaked component-scoped subscriptions and the swallow-all error mapping are real fragility the acceptance tests won't catch.

evidence: app/src/app/core/api.service.ts:18-30 — single small fetch+cache service with a clear contract (get/optional/mediaUrl/spriteFor/getAll)
app/src/app/core/catalog.service.ts:39-137 — CatalogService is a purposeful derived-catalog module, not a god 'utils' layer; pages consume it narrowly

global_abstractions.rationale: The two core abstractions (ApiService, CatalogService) earn their keep with clean boundaries, but runtime config via a window global (server/client coupling) and the triplicated species-id map are the kind of cross-cutting seams a reviewer would ask to close before merge.

readability.rationale: Consistent core/pages/shared layout, accurate naming, small functions and readable templates mean a new teammate finds their way quickly; rough spots are the tri-state loading sentinels, a few casts/duplicated helpers and a stock README.

evidence: app/tsconfig.json:9-17 — strict mode not enabled; every Angular CLI app ships with strict:true since v14, so reviewers must ask why it's off
app/src — zero *.spec.ts files while package.json declares 'ng test' and vitest+jsdom are installed devDependencies (app/package.json:11,32,33)
app/package.json:10 — @angular/forms in dependencies but never imported anywhere in src
app/src/app/pages/pokemon-page.ts:205-304 — the leak/dedup/error-handling round: refCount flag, error conflation and the three duplicated speciesById maps would each be requested changes
review_cost.rationale: Functionally it would ship, but I would not approve as-is: enable strict TypeScript, fix the subscription leak and error conflation, dedupe the species maps, drop the dead dependency, and either add unit tests or remove the test scaffolding — that's a genuine round of changes, not nits.

findings.issue: shareReplay({bufferSize:1, refCount:false}) on component-scoped streams derived from route.paramMap (also lines 212, 249, 304): after PokemonPage is destroyed the source subscriptions are never torn down, retaining the fetch pipeline and cached responses on every visit.
findings.suggestion: Drop shareReplay from component-scoped streams (toSignal already shares per subscription) or use refCount:true; keep refCount:false only for the intentional root-level caches in ApiService/CatalogService.

findings.issue: optional() maps every error — network failures, 500s, timeouts — to null, so a broken API renders 'Not found' pages indistinguishable from genuinely missing resources.
findings.suggestion: Catch only 404 (check HttpErrorResponse.status) and propagate other errors to a distinct error/loading state in the pages.

findings.issue: TypeScript strict mode is disabled in a fresh Angular v22 app where strict is the CLI default; the hand-typed models and casts make this riskier.
findings.suggestion: Enable strict (and strictTemplates) and fix the resulting diagnostics, or document why it was turned off.

findings.issue: No unit tests at all (0 *.spec.ts in src) while the project configures 'ng test' and installs vitest and jsdom.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest specs for the pure logic with real payoff (format.ts helpers, home-page filtering/pagination, buildTables/sorting) — or remove the unused test scaffolding so it doesn't imply coverage that doesn't exist.

findings.issue: DOM scroll is done in a plain effect via setTimeout with no cleanup and a typeof window guard, and re-fires every time the moves tables change.
findings.suggestion: Use afterRenderEffect with a viewChild reference for post-render DOM work, and clear the timer in onCleanup.

findings.issue: The sprite-fallback handler subscribes manually to api.get with no takeUntilDestroyed, no error callback, and a mutable triedFallback flag.
findings.suggestion: Wrap in takeUntilDestroyed(this.destroyRef) (or toSignal) and handle the failure case; derive the flag from a signal if inputs can change.

findings.issue: The speciesById Map-building computed is duplicated verbatim in ability-page.ts:37 and type-page.ts:42, and duplicates what CatalogService already builds in catalog$.
findings.suggestion: Expose a single speciesById signal/observable from CatalogService and inject it in all three pages.

findings.issue: Runtime API config travels through a window.__POKEDEX_API_BASE_URL__ global that server.mjs:16 injects by string-replacing '</head>' in the built index.html — a fragile server/client seam.
findings.suggestion: Have the server emit the value into a data attribute or meta tag and read it via an InjectionToken factory (or APP_INITIALIZER) so the contract is typed and discoverable.

findings.issue: All six route components are eagerly imported; route params are read manually via paramMap instead of withComponentInputBinding, and async reactivity uses RxJS chains rather than the now-stable resource()/httpResource.
findings.suggestion: Use loadComponent per route, provideRouter(routes, withComponentInputBinding()) with input.required<string>() for :name, and resource/httpResource for the per-page fetches — this also deletes the undefined/null sentinel loading logic in the templates.

findings.issue: Moves table rows are tracked with track $index while clicking headers re-sorts the same rows, causing avoidable DOM mutation on every sort.
findings.suggestion: Track by a stable row key such as row.moveName.

summary: A well-structured, accessible Pokédex that passes its acceptance tests with clean core/pages/shared separation, OnPush standalone components and consistent naming. The main merge blockers are previous-generation data loading (RxJS chains plus sentinel-based loading instead of v22's resource/httpResource and input binding), a subscription leak on route-scoped shareReplay streams, error handling that conflates API failures with 404s, and no strict TypeScript or unit tests. I'd ask for one round of changes before approving.
